// FIXTURE - deliberately broken. Stored as .cs.txt so it is never compiled.
// CliInvocationCentralizationGuardTests feeds this file to the same scanner
// that walks runner/** and backend/Features/{Cli,Runner}/**; if the guard ever
// stops reporting it, the guard has gone blunt and the real scan is worthless.
//
// Six separate violations are encoded:
//   1. ProcessStartInfo with FileName = "claude"       -> cli-spawn (nearby identity)
//   2. Process.Start on that start info                -> cli-spawn (nearby identity)
//   3. A spec-driven spawn with NO binary literal      -> cli-spawn (file-scoped identity)
//   4. RUNNER_CLI_BIN read from the environment        -> legacy-env
//   5. ProcessStartInfo with GetCliPath                 -> cli-spawn (indirect identity)
//   6. Process.Start on that indirect start info        -> cli-spawn (indirect identity)
using System.Diagnostics;

namespace AgentRunner;

internal static class NewCodingAgentLauncher
{
    public static Process Launch(string prompt, string repoPath)
    {
        var psi = new ProcessStartInfo
        {
            FileName = "claude",
            WorkingDirectory = repoPath,
            RedirectStandardInput = true,
            RedirectStandardOutput = true,
            UseShellExecute = false,
        };
        psi.ArgumentList.Add("-p");
        var process = Process.Start(psi)
            ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("failed to start the agent CLI");
        process.StandardInput.Write(prompt);
        process.StandardInput.Close();
        return process;
    }

    public static string BinaryFromEnvironment()
        => Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("RUNNER_CLI_BIN") ?? "codex";
}

// The post-T0b shape: the binary name travels inside a serialised invocation
// spec, so nothing quotable is left at the spawn site. Only the file-scoped
// identity rule still recognises this as a coding-agent start.
internal static class SpecDrivenLauncher
{
    public static Task<ProcessResult> RunAsync(DetachedJobSpec spec, CancellationToken ct)
        => ProcessRunner.RunAsync(
            spec.FileName,
            spec.Arguments,
            spec.WorkingDirectory,
            spec.Prompt,
            ct: ct);
}

// The local post-T2 regression shape: the binary path is resolved indirectly,
// so no provider literal and no CliBin option name sits near the process start.
// GetCliPath / ResolveExecutable must still identify it as a CLI launch.
internal static class IndirectPathLauncher
{
    public static Process Launch(GenericCliExecutionService cli, string repoPath)
    {
        var psi = new ProcessStartInfo
        {
            FileName = GenericCliExecutionService.ResolveExecutable(cli.GetCliPath()),
            WorkingDirectory = repoPath,
            UseShellExecute = false,
        };
        return Process.Start(psi)
            ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("failed to start the indirectly resolved agent CLI");
    }
}
